clues.text: This small place lies in the south of Liège in Belgium. It sits at the foot and slope of a hill.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside southern Belgium

source.quote: It is located at the foot and on the slope of a hill in the southern part of Liège, located between the rivers Ourthe and Meuse.

clues.text: In July 2019, heat broke a record here. The air hit 40.2 degrees Celsius, then the hottest ever seen in Belgium.
clues.narrowing: rules out places with no record-breaking summer heat

source.quote: On the 24th of July 2019, during the July 2019 European heat wave, the hottest temperate ever recorded in Belgium at the time was recorded in Angleur, a temperature of 40.2 °C, however this recorded was again broken the next day in the Flemish town of Begijnendijk.

clues.text: This place stood on its own until 1977. In that year, it merged into the city of Liège.
clues.narrowing: rules out places that did not join a larger city in 1977

source.quote: It was a separate municipality until 1977. On 1 January 1977, it was merged into Liège.

clues.text: Two mansions stand down in its lower part. One is called Péralta, and the other is Nagelmackers.
clues.narrowing: rules out places without this pair of named mansions

source.quote: Two mansions can be found in the lower part of Angleur : the Chateau Péralta and the Chateau Nagelmackers

clues.text: Find the science park by the roundabout at Sart Tilman. That hilltop park is the mark of its high part.
clues.narrowing: confirms the place by its hilltop science park

source.quote: The lower part involves an area known as Renory and a railway station called Gare d'Angleur and the higher part is located around the roundabout of Sart Tilman where the Liège Science Park is located.
